items.title: Lesson 2, Check Your Progress, Problem 39: Sketch the velocity-time and position-time graphs for a city bus that (1) pulls away from a stop with a gradual speed-up to 10 m/s in 8 s, (2) cruises at 10 m/s until 24 s, (3) slows to a stop over the next 10 s, (4) waits at a red light until 44 s, (5) speeds up quickly to 12 m/s by 48 s, and (6) cruises at

body.html: In the velocity graph, slope is acceleration. In the position graph, slope at each time equals the velocity at that time.

Velocity graph: a rising line, a flat line at 10 m/s, a falling line to 0, a flat line on the axis, a steeper rise to 12 m/s, and a flat line at 12 m/s. Position graph: a curve bending upward (steeper and steeper), a straight line with a steady slope, a curve flattening out to zero slope, a flat piece while waiting, a curve bending upward quickly, and a steeper straight line. Using areas, the bus is at about 40 m at 8 s, 200 m at 24 s, 250 m at 34 s and 418 m at 60 s.

answer.html: See the graphs above. The 𝑣-𝑡 graph has a rising segment, a flat top, a falling segment to zero, a zero segment, a steeper rise, and a flat top at a higher value. The 𝑥-𝑡 graph is an upward curve, a straight line, a curve flattening to horizontal, a horizontal piece, an upward curve, then a steeper straight line.

check.html: Both graphs share the same time axis, and each 𝑥-𝑡 slope matches the 𝑣-𝑡 height; the bus never moves backward, so the 𝑥-𝑡 graph never slopes down.

items.title: Lesson 2, Check Your Progress, Problem 39: sketch the sprinter's v-t and x-t graphs

body.html: Velocity graph shows slope = acceleration; position graph's slope equals the velocity at each time.

Sequence: walk at constant speed (flat 𝑣-𝑡 line at a small positive value; 𝑥-𝑡 is a straight, gently sloped line); wait (zero velocity; 𝑥-𝑡 flat at the starting blocks); accelerate rapidly (steep rise in 𝑣; 𝑥-𝑡 curves upward, getting steeper); constant maximum velocity (flat line at the top; straight steep 𝑥-𝑡 line, ending at the finish line); slow to a walk over a longer time (gentle downward slope in 𝑣; 𝑥-𝑡 bends over to a gentler slope).

answer.html: See the graphs above (times and speeds are illustrative). The 𝑣-𝑡 graph has a flat low segment, zero segment, steep rise, flat top, and a gentler fall to a walking speed. The 𝑥-𝑡 graph is a gentle line, a flat piece at the starting blocks, an upward-curving piece, a steep straight line reaching the finish line, then a curve flattening to a gentle line.

check.html: Both graphs share the same time axis, and each 𝑥-𝑡 slope matches the 𝑣-𝑡 height.
